items.title: Covista Expands and Strengthens Leadership Bench to Accelerate Purpose at Scale
items.summary: Scott Liles Expands Remit to Lead Corporate Strategy and New Performance Acceleration Office Rick Sinkfield Joins as Vice President of Expansion Covista (NYSE: CVSA), America's largest healthcare educator, today announced an expanded leadership role for Scott Liles and the addition of Rick Sinkfield as Vice President of Expansion, both in support of the company's three-year Purpose at Scale growth strategy built around four core principles: operational excellence, platform extension, employer integration and technology focus. "These moves strengthen our ability to execute our growth strategy in the marketplace," said Steve Beard, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Covista. "Scott and Rick bring the integrated, enterprise-wide thinking and discipline to carry Purpose at Scale forward. Continuing to build our leadership bench now is how we ensure our growth ambitions and our execution stay in lockstep to deliver on our purpose: to open doors and unlock potential." items.title: Chamberlain University to Open Salt Lake City Campus; Now Accepting Applications for Fall 2026
items.summary: Covista, America’s Largest Healthcare Educator, Opening First Utah Location to Help Address State's Critical Nursing Shortage New Campus will be Chamberlain's 26th Location Nationwide Chamberlain University, America’s largest school of nursing and a Covista institution, today announced it will open a new campus in Salt Lake City, Utah. The campus continues Chamberlain's national expansion strategy to address the U.S. healthcare workforce shortage. The university will begin accepting applications on July 21, 2026, with pre-licensure Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) classes beginning October 26, 2026. The announcement comes as the region grapples with one of the most acute healthcare worker shortages in the nation. According to the Covista Care Capacity Monitor , fielded by Gallup, Utah has the lowest number of nurses per capita of any state, just 7 per 1,000 residents, and the gap is widening. items.summary: Awards highlight the company's investment in colleagues, students and the communities it serves Covista (formerly Adtalem Global Education), America's largest healthcare educator, today announced it has been recognized with five prestigious national awards honoring the company's workplace culture, employee experience and commitment to corporate responsibility. items.title: Covista and Advocate Health Launch Strategic Nursing Collaboration to Strengthen Workforce Readiness and Expand Patient Access
items.summary: Innovative new initiative combines education, clinical immersion, financial support and direct employment pathways to expand access and prepare practice-ready nurses Covista (NYSE: CVSA), America's largest healthcare educator, and Advocate Health, the third-largest nonprofit integrated health system in the U.S., today announced a new collaboration to expand access to nursing education and build a direct pipeline of practice-ready nurses across the communities Advocate Health serves. items.title: Chamberlain University to Open Cincinnati Campus, Accepting Applications for Fall 2026
items.summary: Covista, Nation's Largest Healthcare Educator, Opening Cincinnati Campus to Help Address Region's Nearly 50,000 Open Healthcare Jobs Chamberlain University, the nation's largest school of nursing and a Covista institution, today announced it will open a new campus in Cincinnati, Ohio. The Cincinnati campus will be Chamberlain's 25th campus and is one of several new campuses opening in the next year as part of the institution's national expansion strategy. The university is now accepting applications for fall 2026, with pre-licensure Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) classes beginning August 31, 2026. The announcement comes as Ohio works to meet a significant healthcare workforce demand with the state recording nearly 50,000 healthcare vacancies per month last year. That shortage carries real consequences for patients. items.title: Covista Medical Schools Achieve 97% Combined First-Time Residency Attainment Rate
items.summary: AUC and Ross graduates match into family medicine, emergency medicine, psychiatry and other high-need specialties across 42 states. Covista (NYSE: CVSA), America’s largest healthcare educator, today announced a combined 97% first-time residency attainment rate* for its 2025-2026 graduating class at Ross University School of Medicine (RUSM) and American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine (AUC). Graduates will train to become licensed physicians at health systems spanning 42 U.S. states and 26 specialties. AUC’s Class of 2026 achieved over 98% first-time residency attainment rate, and Ross’s Class of 2026 achieved 96%, results that reflect the breadth and competitiveness of two programs built to produce the physicians America needs most. "There are more than twice as many passionate individuals who want to become physicians as there are seats in U.S. medical schools," said Scott Liles, president, medical and veterinary, Covista.
